cells.tense: You are standing in the open moment before anything gets chosen, and you are at ease there.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been holding open and take a single step into it today, small enough that you could stop.
cells.core:
You're in the moment before a choice gets made, and you're not squirming. Most people can't sit there long — they grab the first option so the waiting stops. You stay open, and you can feel what's coming before it's here. That's why the ideas you bring people land; you're describing something they half-sensed and hadn't said yet.

Nothing needs fixing. What this is free to feed next is the other thing: staying somewhere long enough that today's openness turns into something you actually tend. Keep the wonder. Add a little stubbornness. Choose a small version of the thing you can't stop picturing, and stay with it past the interesting part.
cells.sheetLine: You can stay open before you choose. Stay open past the choice too.
cells.verb: sensing what hasn't happened yet and opening to it
cells.place: the moment before anything is chosen

cells.tense: You are bracing at a future that hasn't arrived, and you are spending feeling on what might happen instead of what is.
cells.ask: Catch yourself feeling ahead into one thing that hasn't happened, and put a hand on what's actually here instead. Do that once before the day ends.
cells.core:
You're reading what hasn't happened yet, but hard, ahead of time. Someone's mood, a decision, a conversation you've already run in your head — you've felt it all before it's here, and it's cost you the thing it was for. The open moment turns into a courtroom.

Nothing's wrong with the sensitivity. It's moving faster than the day can carry. What balances it is the slower kind of tending: giving something a bit of room and watching how it actually grows, rather than scripting its ending. So when you notice yourself feeling ahead, come back for one minute and let the thing be undecided. Care that doesn't exhaust is allowed.
cells.sheetLine: You're feeling a future that hasn't happened. Come back to the one happening now.
cells.verb: sensing what hasn't happened yet and opening to it
cells.place: the moment before anything is chosen

cells.tense: You stopped offering what you sensed, and you are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Say the next half-formed thought out loud to someone within the day — awkward, unfinished, exactly as it comes.
cells.core:
The sensing hasn't gone anywhere. What stopped is the offering. The ideas stay in your head now, and the open moment feels less like freedom and more like a room no one's in. When the offering runs, a half-formed thing gets said early and the other person leans in, and the two of you find out together whether it holds. That part is what's quiet — not the imagining, the saying.

What brings it back isn't more imagination. It's letting someone hear a half-formed thing and seeing that they don't run. Not to perform the idea, just to let it exist outside you for a minute. Your sense of what's coming is fine. It's been a while since it had an audience of one.
cells.sheetLine: The sensing is still there. The offering is what stopped.
cells.verb: sensing what hasn't happened yet and opening to it

cells.tense: You are already reading what's coming and calling it something that happens to you, so the pen is down in a room you're already writing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you sensed before it happened and say, out loud, that you were the one who saw it.
cells.core:
This is already running. You feel where a conversation's heading, which idea has legs, what someone's about to say — and then it gets described as the room deciding, or the timing finally being right. The reading happens. The credit goes somewhere else.

What brings it back is the plain kind of discipline: keep a note when a read turns out right, and let that be evidence you can look at instead of a mood you argue with. Not bragging, just bookkeeping. The thing you're best at keeps getting handed to circumstance. Take one of them back and say it was you.
cells.sheetLine: You already read what's coming. Start saying you saw it.
